text: Use /orgs/{ORG-ID}/nonCompliantResources to detect existing violations and remediate them; applying a policy does not automatically rewrite pre-existing configurations. text: Guard optional attributes before comparing them. Cedar skips policies that error during evaluation; MongoDB’s tier example uses has checks. Whether Atlas adds stricter runtime error handling is not established here. (medium confidence) Sources: https://docs.cedarpolicy.com/auth/authorization.html ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-resource-policies.md
keywords: Cedar policy authoring for cluster size and autoscaling caps

text: The minGeneralClassInstanceSizeValue and maxGeneralClassInstanceSizeValue attributes represent the current tier or the minimum and maximum autoscaling sizes; author against these bounds rather than checking only a desired current tier. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-18)
keywords: Cedar policy authoring for cluster size and autoscaling caps

text: Cedar skips policies that error during evaluation. Cedar issue #2428 illustrates incorrect string membership using `in` on a string context attribute (which raises a type error and the policy is skipped), with the corrected idiom being `[...].contains(context.x)`. A Cedar maintainer described it as writing an incorrect policy and not validating it, and the reporter acknowledged it is not an engine bug. This is a general authoring caution, not evidence of an Atlas exploit. Sources: https://docs.cedarpolicy.com/auth/authorization.html ; https://github.com/cedar-policy/cedar/issues/2428
keywords: Cedar policy authoring for cluster size and autoscaling caps

text: A practitioner walkthrough reports successful Terraform deployment and blocked noncompliant requests, but does not demonstrate enforcement of a tier or autoscaling cap. Treat its cap discussion as guidance rather than an independent cap test. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-08-13)
keywords: Cedar policy authoring for cluster size and autoscaling caps

text: Atlas Resource Policies are organization-wide controls that let Organization Owners constrain the cluster configuration options available to developers. They are allow-by-default and apply on top of what a user's Atlas role allows. Specific projects can be excluded, so exceptions are possible. A documented policy type enforces minimum and maximum cluster tiers and auto-scaling sizes. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-resource-policies.md
keywords: Cedar policy authoring for cluster size and autoscaling caps

text: MongoDB explicitly excludes Low CPU and NVMe SSD classes from its sample General class tier restriction; do not describe that sample as a universal instance-size cap. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-18)
keywords: Cedar policy authoring for cluster size and autoscaling caps

text: Atlas accepts forbid policies, excludes permit statements, and allows role-authorized operations by default. Generic Cedar instead defaults to denial without a matching permit; do not transfer its default directly to Atlas. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-18) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-resource-policies.md ; https://docs.cedarpolicy.com/auth/authorization.html
keywords: Cedar policy authoring for cluster size and autoscaling caps

text: Existing autoscaling bounds can exceed a newly introduced policy and continue scaling beyond it, although manual scaling beyond the policy is blocked. Inspect /orgs/{ORG-ID}/nonCompliantResources and reconcile existing bounds. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-18)
keywords: Cedar policy authoring for cluster size and autoscaling caps
